core_obligations: Notation (proof lines 6458-6465): 1_a = the a-fold star product of 1_Y, so d^n_j = 1_j star d star 1_{n-j} and s^n_j = 1_j star s star 1_{n-j}.

Relation (1)(a) with the template computation (lines 6470-6496): for 0 <= i < j <= n+1 both sides of d^n_i d^{n+1}_j = d^n_{j-1} d^{n+1}_i are rewritten via the interchange rule and reduce to 1_i star d star 1_{j-i-1} star d star 1_{n+1-j}; the reduction is displayed in full for the left side and invoked for the right.

Relations (1)(b), (1)(c), (1)(d) (lines 6498-6528): (b) and (d) follow by the same calculus as (a), both sides simplifying to 1_i star d star 1_{j-i-1} star s star 1_{n-j-1} resp. 1_j star s star 1_{i-j-2} star d star 1_{n-i}; (c) - the simplicial identity d_j s_j = d_{j+1} s_j = id - is exactly the first assumption of the lemma.

Relation (1)(e) and the augmentation (lines 6530-6560): for j = i the required identity is the second assumption; for j > i both sides reduce to s star 1_{j-i-1} star s; finally d is an augmentation because d circ (1_1 star d) = d circ (d star 1_1) = d star d.
proof_roadmap: Set up the 1_a shorthand and the interchange rule.
Check the five simplicial relations, (a) in full as the template, (c) and (e) reading off the two assumptions.
Conclude the augmentation property from d star d.
